notes: Spinning-top battles are the game, so Action leads, but Action's own boundary rule hands a fixed field with formal rules to Sports, and a Beyblade dish is exactly that — which is why Sports is named second and why its Physics Sport preset, the physics-ball-in-a-bowl layout, describes each arena better than any avatar-combat preset: a rim containing the tops, fixed launch positions, and a volume that registers the knockout. I swapped that preset's bounded-field shape for world-open and kept all three of its options, because the deliverable is a walkable city containing the arenas rather than a dish on its own; the author's answers hold that to one continuous street-level surface — flat dishes, no overhanging levels, a few blocks around the centre — so it stays P0 rather than picking up the P2 an open-world action city would have brought. The arena count is one central arena plus three smaller satellites in the surrounding blocks, which nothing in the emit form can carry, so it is recorded here. Without a user I decided the shops are storefronts with a menu behind them rather than rooms you walk into, keeping the build off P3, and folded the challenger NPCs and shopkeepers into the city's ambient population; the 1v1, 2v2 and free modes all reuse the same dishes and change no geometry.
